title: cross_field takes the surface_metric connection instead of computing its own vertex frames and transport angles
description:
User design discussion 2026-10-07. NDirectionField (the cross_field node, Knöppel 2013) computes its own discrete connection: vertex tangent frames, angle rescaling so vertex angles sum to 2π, and edge transport angles (its stage timers: compute vertex frames, edge transport angles kappa, compute angle rescaling). The signpost intrinsic triangulation behind ring geodesics holds the same ingredients (signpost angles rescaled by vertex angle sum, reference half-edges, edge lengths). Once CRAW-57's surface_metric node exists, make cross_field take it as an input and express its field in that connection, so the cross field, ring geodesics and cross-field streamlines (CRAW-31) agree on what 'the same direction' means and the frames are computed once. First check the conventions (reference direction per vertex, sign and definition of the transport angle, whether frames are per vertex or per face, the s parameter's use of rescaled angles) and write the mapping on the ticket. The cross field's result values stay a per-element field (MESH-23 attributes are the home for such values); the metric and connection are not forced into the attribute shape.

Convention mapping (NDirectionField on master -> SurfaceMetric). Vertex frame: master took the tangent plane from the summed face normals and x along the mesh's first outgoing half-edge (vertexOutgoingHalfEdgeAt(v, 0)); spoke angles were 3D gaps between spokes sorted by projected angle, rescaled by 2*pi/sum at interior vertices, unscaled at boundary vertices starting after the largest gap, re-zeroed at that first spoke. The metric's frame is intrinsic: reference half-edge vertexReferenceHalfEdge[v] (first half-edge of the fan at a boundary vertex), signpostAngle[h] = corner angles (law of cosines on edge lengths) summed counter-clockwise in fan order, unscaled in [0, vertexAngleSum). Mapping: angleInFrame[h] = signpostAngle[h] * (interior ? 2*pi / vertexAngleSum[v] : 1); master's angle = that minus the same quantity for the first outgoing half-edge, i.e. a per-vertex gauge rotation (u_v -> u_v e^{-i n a0}) that leaves the field unchanged. Vertex transport (Knoeppel): rho_ij = n (angle(h_ji) - angle(h_ij)), no +pi term since n*pi is a multiple of 2*pi for n = 4; same formula, read from the metric. Frames are per vertex for the solve (Knoeppel) and per face for the output (theta, kappa, periodJump in the world-space face frames x_f = mesh.faceHalfEdge); faceX/faceY keep their master definition. kappa (face-to-face) = angle of the twin in face B + pi - angle of the half-edge in face A, the angles inside a triangle from metric corner angles (next side pi - alpha, previous side alpha(axis) - pi); master rotated x_A about the edge by the dihedral, identical in exact arithmetic. The curvature_bias s term uses the per-face holonomy of the rescaled transports, unchanged in form. Vertex-to-face conversion in populate: master projected the vertex direction through world-space vertex frames; now alpha = angle of the corner's half-edge in the face + fieldAngle - its rescaled spoke angle (the metric's vertex-to-corner transport). Angle defect for the singularity index: 2*pi - vertexAngleSum.
definition-of-done: 1. Convention mapping between NDirectionField's frames/transport and the signpost connection written on the ticket. 2. cross_field takes the surface_metric output (optional input; absent, it builds one) and no longer computes its own frames or transport angles. 3. Field equal to today's within a stated angle tolerance on fertility, the rocker arm and the crawfish, with identical singularities (CrossFieldEquivalenceBenchmark). 4. Cross-field time on the crawfish not slower (PATCH-122 baseline 4.4 s). 5. mvn test passes.
testing-plan: 1. CrossFieldEquivalenceBenchmark before/after. 2. Timings on fertility and crawfish.
changes-made: cross_field takes an optional `metric` input (PortType.SURFACE_METRIC). Wire it as `surface = surface_metric(geometry=...)` and then `cross_field(geometry=surface.geometry, metric=surface.metric)`. A metric measured on a different mesh is refused. With no metric, the node builds one with SurfaceMetric.of. No DSL under resources uses cross_field directly. quad_layout (QuadLayoutEngine) takes the no-metric path, so no DSL or RingDslWriter change was needed. NDirectionField.build(mesh, metric) no longer computes any frames or connection of its own. computeVertexFrames, computeAngleRescaling, vertexX/vertexY/vertexNormal/angleDefect and the dihedral-rotation kappa are gone. In their place: angleInFrame = the metric's signpost angle times 2*pi/vertexAngleSum (one pass over the metric's half-edges). kappa is the metric's face-to-face transport, built from corner angles. populate carries each vertex direction into a face with the metric's corner transport instead of projecting through world-space vertex frames. The singularity angle defect is 2*pi - vertexAngleSum. faceX/faceY and the FIELD output keep their master meaning. Also changed: SurfaceMetric.cornerAngle beside a zero-length side now returns pi/2 (pi/3 when every side has collapsed) instead of 0, so a degenerate triangle's angles still sum to pi. Before this fix, every zero-length edge on the crawfish added up to pi of spurious curvature. Tests: new unit.mesh.CrossFieldConnectionTest checks four things on a torus and a disk: kappa equals the face frame rotated about the edge by the dihedral (1e-5); spoke angles equal the 3D corner sums rescaled from the reference half-edge; a wired metric gives the same field as a built one, bit for bit; a metric from another mesh is refused. CrossFieldAssemblyTest passes the metric. CrossFieldEquivalenceBenchmark now measures vertex angles from each vertex's first outgoing half-edge, which removes the gauge choice and keeps master's .angles files comparable. It also records and compares per-face theta (.theta) and writes node times into the report. mvn test: 452 run, 0 failures.

Equivalence: benchmark.CrossFieldEquivalenceBenchmark on load_mesh -> repair_mesh -> cross_field(curvature_bias=-1), with master references recorded before the change. Per-vertex field (the solve): fertility max 1.2e-5 rad, mean 6.9e-8; rockerarm max 1.4e-5, mean 1.2e-7. This is equal within float rounding (float positions; old 3D acos gaps vs. law-of-cosines corners). Raw KCP13 singular triangles are identical: fertility 40/sum -24, rockerarm 20/sum 0. Per-face theta differs: fertility mean 2.4e-3 rad, p50 8e-4, p99 2.4e-2, max 0.52 (inside singular triangles, where the corner mean cancels); rockerarm mean 1.5e-3. The reason is that master projected the rescaled vertex angle through world-space vertex frames, while the new code uses the intrinsic corner transport the solve itself uses. A consequence is that one singularity per model moves to the adjacent corner of the same singular triangle pair: fertility vertex 12889 -> 5054, rockerarm 602 -> 348, both share an edge. Counts are unchanged (40/40, 20/20). This misses DoD 3's 'identical singularities' at vertex level; keeping master's projection would need world-space vertex frames again. Downstream fertility (GridMapPipelineBenchmark/SeamlessPipelineBenchmark, master copy vs this tree): singularities 40/40, 0 flipped, injective, leftover constraints 1607/1607, grid energy after optimisation 3.833e4 -> 3.840e4 (+0.2%), 0 flipped. No regression. Crawfish (IMG_4109 repaired, 469,131 V): the field is not equal to master (vertex angle mean 2.1e-2 rad, median 5e-3). Master's connection was wrong at 651 vertices that a temporary diagnostic found (since removed): 442 fans whose projected-angle sort order differs from the fan order, so master summed gaps between non-neighbouring spokes, and 160 vertices with zero-length edges. Clean meshes show 0 such vertices. Crawfish singular vertices 1460 -> 1444. The vertex-level Poincare-Hopf sum now holds exactly (indexSum4 -80 = 4*chi), against -21 on master.

Timings: surefire JVM, CrossFieldEquivalenceBenchmark node times, 5 runs each, median (runs). The machine was noisy, so per-stage medians are the steadier number. Crawfish cross_field node: master 6229 ms (5075-8127). Unwired (builds its own metric): 5548 (5222-10843). Wired from surface_metric: 4703 (4545-5368), plus surface_metric 208 ms. Crawfish stages, master -> now: kappa 254 -> 100 ms; vertex frames 78 -> gone; angle rescaling 416 -> 19 ms; face frames 40 -> 67; assemble 733 -> 722; solve aligned 3307 -> 3329; populate 723 -> 552. That is about 0.63 s of frame and connection work removed, against 0.21 s to measure the metric. Fertility cross_field node: master 799 ms (695-1627), unwired 759 (709-1424), wired 703 (677-906) + surface_metric 28. Fertility stages: kappa 33 -> 12, vertex frames 15 -> gone, rescaling 44 -> 5, populate 81 -> 64, assemble 81 -> 96 (noise range 48-109 on master), solve 518 -> 485. Rockerarm node 1431 -> 1188.
